claims.claim: Suggested illustrative buyer workflow: Give the traveler a usable departure plan. No private provider contract, actual site design, service entitlement or observed performance inferred. Separate invented timetable: 10-minute pickup + 25-minute travel + 10-minute access/buffer = 45 minutes; a 10 a.m. meeting gives a 9:15 a.m. latest switch.
claims.qualification: Suggested purchaser analysis; all original source dates, access restrictions, legal conditions and unresolved provider-specific facts remain in the article. Timetable inputs are independent of the fare-and-wait comparison and are not provider performance estimates.
claims.recheckTrigger: Change to the proposed itinerary, route, contract, fleet stage, accepted volume or stated model input.

formulas: fallbackSensitivity = (monthlyTrips − fallbackTrips) × autonomousTripCost + fallbackTrips × (fallbackFareUSD + fallbackCoordinationWaitMinutes × minuteValue)
boundaries: Same in-vehicle travel time excluded from both sides.
No productive-work benefit, price observation, cancellation fee, tax difference, comparative safety or real fallback rate assumed.
Only one employee per trip; actual group and assistance needs require a separate comparison.
Fallback share is sensitivity, not probability forecast; missed-deadline consequences remain separate.

updateTriggers: San Antonio expands all-rider admission; Austin changes booking channel or eligible products.
A Texas airport or freeway route obtains documented public booking availability.
A documented Texas employer program changes organizational payment eligibility or terms.
Current route, pickup, fare or support rules materially change the usable trip.
Observed pilot requests, complete door-to-door times and fallback outcomes warrant replacing declared assumptions.
